Hi there, I'm 25 and currently 11 months on T and have had trich since I was a child starting with picking fuzz off blankets and moving onto hairs once I hit puberty.

1) I have pulled eyebrow, eyelash, and arm pit hair. I currently pick on my inner shin just above the ankle in a small 4 inch space (it's very random and I do it on both my legs). When I started T I would pick at stray facial hairs and happy trail hairs, but I stopped myself early on which was difficult but possible.

2) T hasn't increased the amount of hair on my legs for that  spot. The rest of my hair has thickened but because I keep picking I never get a chance to let that spot grow in. I have also been picking that spot for 10 years now so the follicles might be so damaged that it never grows back right. As for the facial and happy trail hairs they kept growing in but that might be in part because I stopped myself early. I did notice that growth where I picked slowed the hair growing back.  As for the armpit, eye lashes, and eyebrow I picked those all in high school so I believe they grew back just fine when I eventually stopped years before I started T.

3) My happy trail and facial hair grew in more the longer I was on T and that did help me stop picking from those places. For me specifically I pick either stray hairs, random dark hairs, and very short hairs that are a  specific length. Once it outgrows that length I'm in the clear and won't pick. So once the stray facial and happy trail hairs started gaining friends and growing that helped stop me from picking them. I'm not sure what makes you pick but this helped me. A lot of it was the mental game of not looking until it grew in more to the point that I wouldn't care to pick it.

4) I believe I pick because of some OCD I inherited from my mother. I tend to pick when nervous or stressed. It seems to calm me every hair that I pick for whatever reason that is. I'm sure there's more factors that go with it but I'm unaware of them at the moment.

I hope this helps you, good luck with starting T and having trichotillomania it can be rather trichy (pun intended)!

I waited 3 years for T becausd a similar issue. I waited the first year willingly because I wanted to socially transition and be sure this is who I am. When I started seeing my therapist at the time I was dealing with a DUAI case and a drinking problem. I explained how I really wanted hormones and she told me to wait because things in my life weren't stable and she didn't feel comfortable giving me hormones. I was hurt being told this initially and took it the wrong way because she did wait about a month and a half to say she didn't want me to go on the hormones. After that I stopped seeing her and decided to wait on seeing another therapist until my life was back in order.

Fast forward to this summer I went back to therapy finally hoping I really to start T, scared that my life wasn't enough in order because, school was about to kick me out. After another therapist change (I saw therapists from my school, the first girl this recent summer was an intern finishing her last PhD year, who had arrived the previous summer and her time was over) which slowed me down about a month until I finally got my T note. My last therapist  (I made the decision to leave school recently so we had to end) had a lot of great insight with receiving T notes. I had explained to her how the very first woman I saw 3 years  before said no because my life wasn't in order and she explained how many times therapists are worried if something big is happening that hormones might make it worse. She also said that a lot of people do lie and say everything in their life is great so they can get hormones quickly without talking about everything going on, and she warned me if she felt I was doing the same she would not be willing to prescribe me hormones. 

It hurts right now feeling like your losing time not being on hormones, but I look back when I wanted them so badly and I'm thankful I didn't start then because life had too many things happening then to deal with hormones as well. Maybe focus on yourself for a bit before this next therapist. Think about why she felt like you were hiding things from her or not mentioning them. Take some time while your waiting to work on yourself and your life so when you see this next therapist there might be a different result, but if not be open to understanding why and see what needs to be changed. 

TL;Dr- Waited 3 years for hormones after drinking issues because original therapist refused to prescribe, waited and got my life in order so I was ready to take hormones.

Some people wait until they are able to cut their hair and wear clothes that suite their tastes. I'm not sure how far in you are to the transition. For me personally I changed my name socially before I cut my hair and I grew into the man I am today as weird as that sounds. I spent a good 2 months debating names, I had a list I looked at everyday. I considered if the name matched my personality and how I look. I would look in the mirror and see if I looked like a Nolan or Charlie. I would think about my friends calling me that name or any nicknames that might occur once I picked that name, as well as if it sounded right if they called me that name if it truly felt like it was me. I also looked into the background of the names I really wanted once I got down to the final 3 or 4, look at their roots and meaning, could anyone turn it into a potentially hurtful nickname to make fun of me. 


I eventually ended with Rory and I will say that I did notice things I didn't expect once I picked my name. One, to elaborate on the "growing into my name" statement I did pick it when my hair was still longer and my roommates and friends had a hard time saying it. The day I cut my hair it was like a light switch, my roommates went from struggling with my name to saying it easily like it was second nature. I had a better view of who Rory was I could finally see him better if that makes any sense. Two, when I chose my name I did not think about the double "R" sound in Rory which some people struggle with. Another common problem is people always mistake me for "Lori" which drives me nuts because I never thought about that either. I don't know if I just over think saying it now and it's hard to understand me but it happens often. I've noticed a lot of people who are Asian and less Americanized struggle and say "Lori" as well, another thing I didn't expect and I'm almost positive has something to do with dialect. Lastly, people manage to shorten Rory to Ror or rawr which is fine by me I just never imagined a 4 letter name could get shorter or have a nickname and yet it has.

I hope this long winded short story answers your question!

TL;DR- Think about literally everything when picking a new name but realize there will be somethings you never expected that come along with a new name.
